end.summary:
Arjun practised factorising x² + px + q by finding two numbers.
They got 4 of 6 unaided attempts correct and used sum/product checks.
They took out common factors correctly in 2 of 2 attempts, including 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3).
The mix-up of copying 5 and 6 into the brackets was corrected later by checking the sum and product.
Teach-back was not passed; rectangle tiles were not completed.
end.parentNote: Arjun practised finding two numbers whose sum and product match the middle and constant terms, and taking out a common factor. They explained the common-factor method by multiplying back to check 3(2x + 3) = 6x + 9. They first wrote (x + 5)(x + 6) for x² + 5x + 6, but later corrected this to (x + 2)(x + 3) using the sum-and-product check. At home, practise a few examples by writing the required sum and product beside each expression before choosing the brackets.
